made: 2026-10-30, Mac mini, scripts in the session scratchpad (op_score.py, op_eval.py, op_diag2.py)
method: E3 scored on every stream at a 20 ms hop; each of the five 100 ms phases replayed through the deployed rule (score every 100 ms on the newest 1.0 s, spot when P >= threshold, spotter deaf 1.0 s after a spot, answers at least 1.5 s apart). Counts are means over the five phases. Recall match: each answer counts for at most one call, -0.3..1.6 s from the labelled onset (primary); train_mochi's 0.2..1.6 s criterion also reported (it scores E3's early, 0.1 s after onset, answers as misses). Two-stage: answer at P >= 0.9, or when a run of scores >= T2 starts 1.0-5.0 s after the start of an earlier run >= T2; run memory cleared by every answer. Offline replay cannot model the pause while a head take runs or the zeroed input during quacks, so false wakes are an upper bound.

extra_answers_vs_single_0.9_on_home_life.pool: life_1030 evening + late + live segments, live_150103, own_quacks_144713 (about 0.64 h per replay, five replays)

recommendation.reason: At 18:53 (Shawn's calls as the stated assumption) it answers 2.0-2.2 s after the first call at 4 of 5 phases (deployed: 7.6 s, the third call); held-out LibriSpeech 0 in 2.3 h, synthetic speech 0, RoboClub conversation 0 in 5 min, held-out room spans 0; extra answers on home life negatives about +2.8/h. Single 0.8 also answers at 18:53 but adds about +11.6/h on the same home negatives. Without the 18:53 assumption no rule measurably beats single 0.9 on recall (72.6 to 76.2 of 99 labelled calls), so the case rests on that episode and Shawn's report that he called several times.
